ERAN Sanggunjang Panlungsod Member Sipalay City proxnnee Of Negros Occidental Dear SP Member Eran: Thts has reference to your letter dated 25 November 2024 seeking this Department's guidance and legal opinion on the following matters. 1. Is it legal for the Barangay Captain and Barangay Treasurer to withhold copies of disbursement vouchers if these are requested by concerned citizens? 2. Is it legal for the Barangay Captain and Barangay Treasurer to willfully refuse to post copies of the disbursement vouchers on the Barangay Full Disclosure Board as required under the Full Disclosure Policy? 3. Are the Barangay Captain and Barangay Treasurer administratively liable for failing to provide copies of the disbursement vouchers and/or willfully refusing tc post these documents on the Full Disclosure Board? As to the first guerv, we answer in the negative. At the onset, it is not legal for the Punong Barangay and Barangay Treasurer to withhold copies of disbursement vouchers when requested by concerned citizens, provided that the request complies with the law and proper procedures. In connection with this, Section 3521 of RA 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 , mandates the full disclosure of financial transactions of local government units (LGUs), including barangays. Barangays are also required to post financial documents, including disbursement vouchers, in public places and make them accessible to citizens. Further, Section 5 (e) of RA 6713, otherwise known as the "Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees" states that all public documents must be made accessible to, and readily available for inspection by, the public within reasonable working hours. Section 352. Posting of the Summary Of Income and Expenditures. - Local treasurers, accountants, budget officers, and Other accountable officers shall, within thirty (30) days from the end of the fiscal year, post in at least three (3) publicly accessible and conspicuous places in the local government unit a summary of all revenues collected and funds received including the appropriations and disbursements of such funds during the preceding fiscal year. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Thus, the Punong Barangay and Barangay Treasurer cannot legally withhold copies of disbursement vouchers from concerned Citizens who properly request them. as these are public documents As to the we will answer them in one discussion as they are interrelated It is not also legal for the Punong Barangay and Barangay Treaqurer to willfully refuse to post copies of disbutsement vouchers on the Barangay Full Disclosure Board. as required under the Full Disclosure Policy (F DP) Doing 30 violates multiple laws and regulations promoting transpmency and accountability in government transactions In addition to Section 352 of the LGC, DILG Memorandum Circular No 2024-021? provides that under the Full Disclosure Policy, local governments are to fully disclose particular financial documents in at least three (3) conspicuous places and In the FDP Portal. to keep their constituents informed on how the LOU budget is managed disbursed and used. Further, RA 6713 mandates transparency and public access to offeal documents to prevent corruption. Thus, the Punong Barangay and barangay treasurer refuse to post the appropriate finanaal documents on the full disclosure board as required by the abovementioned laws, they may face administrative charges for neglect of duty, misconduct, or abuse of authority under the LGC. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very tuly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELWRPB/LLLS-LRAL1-onasm Copy furnished LEOCADIO T.
